headline: Software Holds the Line as Sellers Hit Almost Every Other Corner of the Market
body_html:
Wednesday's session, the final trading day of the third quarter, ended on a decidedly cautious note. Of 544 stocks tracked, 345 fell against 198 that managed a gain, leaving the tape tilted firmly to the downside. The most punishing declines were concentrated in Homebuilders, off 1.21%, and Industrials, down 0.86%, suggesting investors used the quarter-end to pare cyclical exposure. Consumer and Healthcare names also struggled, dropping 0.65% and 0.60% respectively, as the defensive bid that traders might have expected simply failed to materialize.

The lone sector to finish in positive territory was Software, which edged up 0.54% — a narrow but meaningful hold. Qualys climbed 5.00%, Synopsys added 4.57%, ZoomInfo rose 4.13%, and UiPath gained 4.06%, forming a coherent cluster of enterprise-software strength that stood apart from the broader retreat. Semiconductors and Materials were essentially flat, while Energy slipped 0.21%.

The session's undisputed standout was Rogers Corp, the electronic-materials specialist, which surged 11.24% to lead every name in the universe. FormFactor, in semiconductor equipment, followed with a 9.57% advance. On the other end, Jabil collapsed 9.54%, the sharpest single-stock loss of the day, serving as a pointed reminder that contract electronics manufacturing remained deeply out of favor as the quarter drew to a close.

briefs.headline: Rogers Corp Surges More Than 11% to Lead the Universe
briefs.body: Electronic-materials maker Rogers Corp posted a gain of 11.24% on Wednesday, the largest advance among all tracked names. The move attracted attention on the final day of the quarter, when outsized single-stock moves can reflect both fresh conviction and end-of-period repositioning by institutional accounts.

briefs.headline: Jabil Slides Nearly 10%, Deepest Loss of the Session
briefs.body: Contract electronics manufacturer Jabil shed 9.54%, standing out as the session's worst performer by a wide margin. The decline underscored persistent pressure on the electronics-manufacturing segment even as certain technology sub-sectors managed to hold their footing heading into quarter-end.

briefs.headline: Wall Street Books a Strong Quarter Despite a Soft Final Day
briefs.body: Even as Wednesday's tape leaned negative, the broader market closed out the third quarter on solid overall footing. Quarter-end portfolio adjustments appeared to weigh on cyclical and consumer names in particular, with investors locking in gains from earlier in the period ahead of the new quarter.

briefs.headline: MGM's Chief Executive Signals Openness to Casino Consolidation Talks
briefs.body: MGM Resorts' chief executive left the door open to a potential bid involving People Inc. as deal activity in the casino sector heats up. The comments suggest consolidation appetite remains alive in the gaming industry, which has been navigating a shifting consumer-spending environment and evolving regulatory landscape.

briefs.headline: Aviation Authorities Heighten Scrutiny After Midair Security Incident
briefs.body: Global aviation regulators responded after passengers reportedly foiled an attempt to crash a Dubai-to-Tel Aviv flight involving a confrontation between pilots. Israel said it would expand pilot-screening procedures, and the EU's aviation agency separately issued an advisory regarding Saudi airspace following a series of Houthi drone attacks on the region.

briefs.headline: Mattel Taps Roger Lynch to Lead Toymaker Into New Chapter
briefs.body: Mattel named Roger Lynch as its incoming chief executive, replacing Ynon Kreiz in the company's top role. Lynch, known for his digital-media background, takes the helm of one of the world's largest toy companies at a moment when the consumer landscape and licensing dynamics are under considerable competitive pressure.
